title: Collusion-Secure Semi-Quantum Secret Sharing Scheme using a Quantum Third Party
abstract: The security of a secret sharing protocol is compromised if one or more dishonest participants can reconstruct the secret by deviating from the prescribed protocol, particularly when such malicious behavior remains undetected. Semi-Quantum Secret Sharing (SQSS) is a variant of secret sharing in which the participants possess only classical capabilities, such as preparing and measuring qubits in the computational ($Z$) basis, while a quantum-capable third party assists the dealer in generating and distributing quantum shares of a classical secret. The limited quantum capabilities of the participants in SQSS protocols may introduce vulnerabilities to collusion attacks, enabling an assisting quantum third party, in collaboration with a dishonest classical participant, to jointly recover the secret even without detection. In this work, we propose a novel SQSS protocol that eliminates this vulnerability and achieves information-theoretic security against collusion attacks. We further prove that the proposed protocol is secure against a broad class of external and internal attacks. Finally, a comparative analysis demonstrates that our construction advances existing SQSS protocols by simultaneously optimizing qubit efficiency, involves a classical dealer, and resilience against DCNA attacks using basic Bell states.
summary: This paper introduces a robust Semi-Quantum Secret Sharing (SQSS) protocol designed to eliminate critical security vulnerabilities present in prior schemes. By incorporating decoy states and restricting operational authority, the authors achieve information-theoretic security against sophisticated collusion attacks. This advances the practical application of quantum key distribution concepts to secure multi-party computation.
main_problem: The security of Semi-Quantum Secret Sharing (SQSS) protocols is vulnerable to undetected collusion attacks by dishonest participants, even when assisted by a quantum third party.
main_result: The authors propose a novel SQSS protocol that achieves information-theoretic security against collusion attacks and is resilient against various external and internal eavesdropping strategies.
method: The work involves designing a multi-phase quantum protocol incorporating decoy states, restricting operational authority, and using error rate checks (QBER) to detect malicious behavior.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum communication protocol involving classical participants with limited quantum capabilities (Z-basis measurements) assisted by a quantum third party, utilizing entangled pairs and decoy states.
key_observables: Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER), detection probability of attacks (e.g., DCNA), and the final reconstructed secret key.
important_parameters: Qubit efficiency ($\eta$), the number of decoy particles ($m_X$), and the threshold for QBER.
main_assumptions: The security proofs rely on the assumption that the protocol structure restricts the authority of the third party and that operational modes are announced only after all measurements are complete.
figures_summary: The notes mention a comparison table (Table 1) summarizing the proposed protocol's advantages over existing schemes regarding security and efficiency, and a trace table (Table 2) detailing an attack simulation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first identifying vulnerabilities in existing SQSS protocols, then proposing an enhanced, multi-phase protocol, followed by rigorous security proofs against specific attacks (DCNA, EM, DSSA), and finally demonstrating the recovery of the secret under a universal Z-sweep attack.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the security foundations of quantum information protocols, which is central to quantum computing and quantum cryptography research.
